title: Adaptive-Precision Kernel Adapter & Prefill/Decode Scheduler
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: We observe ~8-20% token-latency regressions on short decoding requests when using INT8/FP8 optimized kernels due to dequantization and layout conversion overheads during prefill/decoding transitions. Goals: (1) reduce overall per-token latency regressions for mixed-precision paths, (2) avoid adding memory pressure that increases GC/host-mm overhead, (3) maintain inference cost savings from quantized kernels wherever beneficial. Scope: implement an adaptive kernel adapter layer that picks between quantized and FP16 decode pipelines at runtime and a prefill/decode scheduler that minimizes layout conversions and KV cache churn.
background: We already have optimized static INT8 and FP8 kernel implementations and profiling hooks. Prior tickets focused on kernel-level optimizations (quant-routing, dequant fusion). However, production traces show most regressions are not pure kernel compute time but the orchestration around prefill vs decode: repeated format conversions, redundant dequant steps, and inefficient KV copy patterns while switching execution paths. Also attention fusion variants (fused QKV vs separate) interact with memory layout expectations making naive path switching expensive.
proposal: 1) Kernel Adapter: introduce a lightweight runtime decision point per request that considers: model variant (quantized or full-precision), request length, batch size, and recent decode latency/error metrics. The adapter can: - Prefer quantized path for long prefill-heavy workloads where token cost dominates. - Prefer FP16 decode for sub-50 token decode-only requests where conversion overhead outweighs compute savings. 2) Prefill/Decode Scheduler: coalesce format conversions by scheduling prefill and short decodes to reuse existing tensor layouts and KV cache buffers. Add a staged conversion (lazy dequant) where we delay dequant until first compute that absolutely requires FP16 values. 3) Attention Path Compatibility: add minimal layout adapters that translate between fused-QKV and separate-QKV kernels without full copy when possible (pointer-steering, view-based aliasing). 4) Metric gates: enable dynamic thresholds that can be tuned per-deployment (region/tier) to prioritize latency vs cost.
design_decisions: - Decision 1: Use runtime heuristics rather than compile-time model tagging so thresholds can be tuned without redeploying models. - Decision 2: Implement lazy dequant (defer conversion) instead of full fusion across prefill/decode because it minimizes code complexity and is backwards compatible. - Decision 3: Keep adapter logic pluggable to allow future ML-driven routing (RL/learned thresholds).
tradeoffs: - Latency vs Cost: preferring FP16 increases cost but can reduce tail latency for short requests. - Complexity: adaptive logic introduces more code paths and test cases. - Memory: lazy dequant may hold duplicate buffers briefly; need eviction policies to avoid OOM.
benchmarks_plan: Microbenchmarks: create synthetic workloads with varying prefill lengths (0, 8, 64, 512 tokens), batch sizes (1,4,16), and decode lengths (0-64). Measure p50/p95/p99 latency, per-token time, and GPU memory. Compare baseline (always-quantized), always-FP16, and Adaptive-Adapter. Target: p95 decode latency improvement of >=10% over always-quantized on short requests, and <=3% regression on long prefill-heavy workloads. Cost model: compute tokens/sec and estimated $/1M tokens.
implementation_notes: - New module: runtime/adapter/precision_adapter.cc + python shim for thresholds. - Scheduler changes in runtime/scheduler: add buffer pool semantics and a 'layout token' meta field. - KV cache: change eviction policy to be layout-aware (mark cold buffers for conversion). - Metrics: add 'precision_path' tag to perf traces and per-request billing logs. - Tests: unit tests for adapter thresholds, integration tests with small transformer models (gpt-lite), and canary rollout with 5% traffic.
experiments_so_far: 2025-11-14: prototype lazy dequant + single layout reuse on A100: p95 decode for 8-token requests improved 15% vs baseline quant (absolute p95 42ms -> 36ms).
2025-11-16: pointer aliasing between fused-QKV and separate-QKV avoided one copy in 60% of prefill patterns; p50 improved 7%.
2025-11-18: memory overhead observed at batch size 16 for lazy-dequant ~120MB increase; added eviction threshold heuristics.
Notes: prototype ran on nightly branch (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/781).
open_risks: - Edge cases where model ops require immediate FP16 (custom ops) could bypass lazy path and cause incorrect outputs if not detected. - Numeric quality regression risk: need quality evals on quantized->lazy-dequant path against standard eval prompts. - Canary rollback semantics need clear instrumentation to avoid customer-facing regressions.
next_steps: Finalize adapter API and add feature flag: precision_adapter.v1 (runtime-config)
Add full integration tests including cross-model attention layout variants
Run 1 week canary on staging with traffic shaping: 5% -> 20% -> 100% if no regressions
Performance dashboards: add per-path cost/latency broken down by request shape
acceptance_criteria: - p95 decode latency for short requests improved >=10% vs always-quantized on 3 target models (gpt-medium, gpt-large, code-optim). - No quality regression >0.5% on standard regression test set. - Memory overhead under control: <200MB extra on 16-batch workloads. - Canary metrics show no SLO violations after 72h.
